title: Polylog-depth Quantum Thermal Simulation via Local Recovery Channels
authors: Hideaki Hakoshima, Atsushi Iwaki, Nobuyuki Yoshioka
abstract: We establish sufficient conditions for preparing quantum thermal states of noncommuting local Hamiltonians with polylogarithmic circuit depth in arbitrary fixed spatial dimension. Our conditions combine locality and stability bounds on the effective interactions of reduced density matrices of a Gibbs state with a quantitative high-temperature condition and access to coarse classical reference Hamiltonians. When these references can be generated locally, the classical preprocessing cost is $N^{1+o(1)}$ for $N$ sites at inverse-polynomial global accuracy. We construct the preparation circuit from spatially localized Petz recovery maps. Quantum corrections derived from the microscopic Hamiltonian enable accurate recovery while the classical references remain coarse. After preprocessing, the resulting circuit prepares the canonical purification using $N\operatorname{polylog}(N/\varepsilon)$ gates and qubits, where $\varepsilon$ is the preparation error. These results link two fundamental questions: how correlations are organized in thermal equilibrium, and how efficiently the corresponding states can be realized through operations allowed by quantum mechanics. By translating static equilibrium structure into explicit preparation circuits, they give equilibrium locality a constructive computational interpretation and a physically grounded role in quantum algorithm design.
summary: This work develops a method to efficiently prepare quantum thermal states for complex, interacting quantum systems. By combining classical approximations for the bulk of the state with localized quantum corrections, the authors achieve a circuit depth scaling only polylogarithmically with system size. This bridges the gap between the theoretical understanding of equilibrium correlations and the practical limits of quantum computation.
main_problem: The paper establishes sufficient conditions for preparing quantum thermal states of noncommuting local Hamiltonians with polylogarithmic circuit depth.
main_result: They provide a constructive method to translate the static structure of thermal equilibrium into explicit quantum circuits with resource scaling of polylog(N/epsilon) depth.
method: The approach combines coarse classical reference Hamiltonians with quantum corrections derived from localized Petz recovery maps to approximate the full Gibbs state preparation.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum many-body system on N sites governed by a local Hamiltonian, targeting the canonical purification of the Gibbs state ($ho \propto e^{- eta H}$).
key_observables: Preparation error ($\epsilon$), circuit depth ($	ext{polylog}(N/\epsilon)$), and classical preprocessing cost ($N^{1+o(1)}$).
important_parameters: Inverse temperature ($ eta$), preparation error ($\epsilon$), and system size ($N$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on locality and stability bounds for effective interactions, and the availability of local classical reference Hamiltonians.
figures_summary: Table I compares various Gibbs-preparation methods based on their assumptions and resource bounds (Depth). Figure 1 illustrates the locality and constructive implementation of a one-site Petz recovery.
paper_structure: The argument progresses from establishing general local recovery techniques to achieving efficient circuit implementation by factorizing the operator representation using classical references, culminating in the explicit construction of quantum corrections via sequential deletion steps.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, computationally bounded pathway to simulate thermal equilibrium states, which is a cornerstone problem in non-equilibrium and open quantum systems.
